utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, can you please put -- go back and put the 1s on again for the place where the trucks arrived; the 2 where -- the house which you secured for yourself.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that clear now?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that receive an MFI 169?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Re, that will be MFI 169.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we now turn to Prosecution Exhibit 7. Mr. Arnautovic, do you recognise that photograph as an enlargement of the section of the photograph you just marked a moment ago, which was Exhibit P3?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see in that photograph the house in which -- which you secured for yourself?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does that also show the place where the trucks arrived?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just so we have the same marking, can you please mark with a 1 and a circle where the trucks arrived.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A 2 for the house which you secured.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you possibly put the circle a bit larger so there's more space between the figure and the circle. The house at the bottom, that was the one you marked with a 3 before. Is that correct? Where Adnan Solakovic's soldiers were staying.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: This house here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. There's a house above that. Were any soldiers accommodated in that house?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which soldiers were they?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Of the 9th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many soldiers to your knowledge were accommodated in that particular house?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, there were five or six soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there were any Croat residents in that particular house when the soldiers went there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I remember -- I remember two women and a male.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what happened to them when the soldiers came to get accommodated or to seek accommodation in that particular house? Do you know what their response was?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: They complained, too, that they were not willing to allow anyone in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please mark that house with a 4.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the house below that you've marked number 3 were the Croats living there or staying there when the soldiers from the ABiH sought accommodation?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what happened there because Adnan Solakovic's men arrived there before us. I don't know if there had been anyone in that house before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And can you see on this photograph the place where the meeting between Mr. Karic and high-ranking officers and men from -- lower-ranking soldiers which are colloquially called as your men - the men you were with - took place. Is that on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please mark that area with as large a circle as you need to do and a 5.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: This is where the troops were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you've drawn a half circle, a sort of crescent. Where were the --

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: That's how the troops were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where you've put the 5, are you indicating that's where Mr. Karic was standing, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the place. There were a terrace of some sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the troops were standing in a semicircle, grouped around him when he was addressing you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that 5 clear enough for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's okay for me. I notice Mr. Morrissey is nodding, so there's no problem on their part.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can that be received into evidence as MFI 170, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. There's no objection. So this document as well as 169 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the response of the soldiers to Mr. Karic's remark about throwing the civilians into the river?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Some of them laughed and said, No problem, when he said, If anybody's putting up resistance just throw them into the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your own personal response?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I personally found it strange to hear that because I could feel that something was wrong. There must be some sort of trick, snag.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you heard it, did you consider it to be an order?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: The way it was said - and it was said in front of troops who lost relatives, family members, et cetera - and you didn't need to tell them twice, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: There were some among the troops whose families were wiped out or who lost loved ones, et cetera, and who were not reluctant to settle personal scores.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you concerned because of your knowledge of the soldiers' personal circumstances as to the effect -- as to what might happen when Mr. Karic said that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: It's not so much that I was concerned. I was more concerned because there were many units, not only Adnan Solakovic. There was the Handzar Division, there were other units. There were also former camp inmates from western Mostar. And the atmosphere was such that anything could happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do after Mr. Karic had said that to the assembled soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I did nothing. I asked the logistics for some mattresses for people to find whatever accommodation in the houses they could make, improvise, even crammed, pending combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you get the mattresses from?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: From Zuka's logistics unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Jablanica or in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: In Jablanica in the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: After Mr. Karic's remark about throwing the civilians in the river, did you travel to Jablanica, to Zuka's base?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Once again, I object to leading on matters that may become of some importance; this is clearly one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: With respect, it's not leading. It's a question: Did you go there? The witness can answer yes, no. I'm not suggesting he did go there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You can ask, what did you do after that? This is more neutral, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, you've told the Trial Chamber that you were in Jablanica in the morning before you went to Grabovica and you've just said Mr. Karic made a remark about throwing some civilians in the river. Did you at any stage in that day as logistics officer return to the base in Jablanica or did you remain in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I went several times between Jablanica and Grabovica. I made several trips there and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Having heard -- I withdraw that. Where was Ramiz Delalic on the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Ramiz had stayed back in Konjic to purchase some weapons, supplies, and later he came to the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this has got to stop. Let the witness say where the headquarters was and don't tell him, in my submission, where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I didn't think it's an issue that Zuka as based in Jablanica, and the witness has already said he was there and that was where the headquarters were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The witness answered that later he came to the headquarters. And then you asked that's in Jablanica? I think there's no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The headquarters, were they in -- are they the ones you're referring to as Zuka's base in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see Ramiz Delalic in Jablanica at the headquarters on that day?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: He arrived sometime towards the evening because he had spent the entire day in Konjic and he arrived at the headquarters in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you meet him on that day he headquarters in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I saw him. I naturally dropped by for coffee. He was there together with Malco Rovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you discuss with anyone else what Mr. Karic had said to you about throwing the civilians in the river?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when I came to get the mattresses, I chatted with them and I said, By the way, you had told me that the accommodation was taken care of, but that wasn't true. It was all empty talk. You said it was all taken care of and it wasn't. But I didn't go into detail -- I didn't tell that story in detail because there was some people around whom I didn't know that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just going back to your last answer. I'll break it down. When you came to get the mattresses, are you referring to mattresses stored at Zuka's base, the logistics section in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said "I chatted with them." Who is them?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Zuka's soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you tell anyone in a higher position than you were as logistics officer about what Mr. Karic had said?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said Mr. Karic had made a remark about throwing the civilians into the river when he was addressing a large group of soldiers. After that did you discuss with or tell anyone of a position higher than you in the army what Mr. Karic had said?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in Jablanica in Zuka's headquarters, I told them about it. When Ramiz and Malco Rovcanin were there, I said there was some sort of misunderstanding; there's no accommodation there or anything. I complained to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you tell them what Mr. Karic had said about throwing the civilians in the river?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned that that was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that to Ramiz Delalic and Malco Rovcanin?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I told Ramiz, and there was some others there from Zuka's men, Nihad or Nihko was there and four or five others.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was their response to what you said?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: When I told them that, I said, Well, I've come to fetch some mattresses and we'll manage somehow; everything will be all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you get the mattresses?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you take them back to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you stay in Grabovica on the night of the 8th? That's the first night you arrived there.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I stayed there -- I went back and forth three or four times to get everything that the soldiers needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you stay in the house which you marked I think with a 2 before on MFI 169 and MFI 170 were the exhibit numbers?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do the next morning, that's the 9th of September -- before we come to that, who did you stay with in the white house -- sorry, the white house marked number 2?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was there; Elvedin Music was there; Hajric, a young man who was killed later; and another man, I can't recall his name now, who guarded the things I had brought there, the weapons and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened the next morning? That's the morning of the 9th of September.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I went to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you go to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I went there because I had some business to take care of regarding the security of the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you return to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many times did you go between Grabovica and Jablanica on the 9th?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I can't recall precisely. Two or three times I had a car, so I went back and forth because they were getting ready to go into action, to go into battle.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the business you had to take care of regarding the security of the men?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I had to get packed lunches for them so that they would be ready to go into action.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you stay on the second night? That's the night of the 9th of September.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you stay in Jablanica that night?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: There was an agreement there about a meeting. They were discussing the attacks and all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Ramiz was there, the people from the corps, Zuka, Sefer was there I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sefer, who's Sefer?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sefer's his given name. What's his family name?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you participate in these meetings or did you only hear about them?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. I remained outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were these meetings taking place?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: In Zuka's headquarters. There was some sort of coffee bar there, and behind there were two other rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now about the next day, which was the 10th of September, 1993. You said you stayed overnight in Jablanica. The previous day you had travelled between Grabovica and Jablanica several times. Did you return to Grabovica on the 10th of September?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At approximately what time did you go there and who did you go there with?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were -- I don't know. It might have been 9.00 or 10.00 I went with Ramiz Delalic, I set out with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How far did you get?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: We set out from Jablanica and we had arrived to a point just before Grabovica. That was the first time that he was going there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At what point did you arrive to? Are you saying you stopped on the way?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: We were going from Jablanica in the direction of Grabovica by car, but there is a kind of barrier or checkpoint in front of the entrance where there was soldiers. We stopped there and Crni, one of our fighters, said he had found two children, two brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This checkpoint which was in front of the entrance and where there were soldiers, was that a checkpoint that was there on the previous occasions you've been between Grabovica and Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a barrier to prevent men from getting in because there was only this one entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many soldiers were on this checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: There was some in the house and some at the barrier. There were five or six staying there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying there was a house near the checkpoint and the soldiers were staying in that house adjacent to the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you able to say from which unit those soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was near Adnan Solakovic's. There were two or three who were to be in charge of the action and a few of ours. And Cedo's Wolves and the Handzar Division were there before you come to the checkpoint and the black wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that Crni said he had found two children, two brothers. What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: He said, I found these two brothers in the woods, and they say that their grandfather, their grandmother, their mother, their sister have all been killed and they managed to escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your response and Ramiz Delalic's response to being told this?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I know Ramiz well. His response was fierce. He immediately started an investigation to find out what had happened and who had killed those people. He asked them if they would be able to recognise if any of the men were the perpetrators, whether they would recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Crni told you he found two children, two brothers, did you and Ramiz see the two brothers or speak to the two brothers?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you find them?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Near the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was it then that Ramiz Delalic asked the boys if they would be able to recognise the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He asked them that then. He was very angry. We didn't know what had actually happened until he questioned them about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did you and Ramiz Delalic do with these children after speaking with them?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Ramiz lined up the men; he was very angry at the men. He yelled at them and they were all saying, We don't know anything about it, we don't know anything about it. And he was saying, How come you don't know anything about it. He lined up the unit. One of the boys said that he remembered the face of the man who killed his family and that he would recognise him at once.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was it he lined up the men?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: They lined them up near the house where I was staying. There is a meadow there and he lined them all up there for them to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that the point where you put a 1 on the two photographs MFI 169 and 170 earlier where the trucks stopped?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Where he lined up the men, it's where number 2 is. On the right-hand side of that house there is a meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Approximately how many men did he line up and how did he line them?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: He lined them up in a single line, but there are only five or six men there at the time because some had gone to reconnoitre because there was an action being prepared so that some men were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know a man called Enes Sakrak?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I can't recall the name now. I can't recall the face -- or rather, I heard about the name later on but I can't remember what he looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was one of the men in the line-up?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the a man called Mustafa Hota, did you know him at the time?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he in the line-up?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Should he have been?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: They should all have been there except for the ones who went to do reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know where -- was Mustafa Hota on reconnaissance duties when the line-up was being held?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that he wasn't there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you hear about where he was?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: That he had gone up into the woods somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you hear about the reason why he'd gone up into the woods somewhere?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Nobody said anything about it. Everybody pretended to be surprised when they heard about these events. They all pretended they didn't know anything about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were the boys there when Ramiz Delalic lined up the men in front of the house?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How old were the boys?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, one of them said he was 11 and the other one 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they able to or did they indicate that they recognised any of the men in the line-up as the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: They didn't recognise anyone at that time. This boy said he remembered the man well and he would have recognised him, and he said that he was not any of the men in the line-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you and Ramiz Delalic do with the children after the line-up?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: We took them to Zuka's headquarters in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did Ramiz Delalic go and where did you go and what did you do with the children when you got there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed in front of the headquarters and Ramiz Delalic went in. He went into Zuka's headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the children?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: They stayed in front with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did Ramiz Delalic go to?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: He went to Zuka's office to see about these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you able to hear what he was saying, if anything, when he went to Zuka's office?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: He went there and he was very angry because he'd heard about the murders. He didn't know the number of murders that had taken place. He went into the coffee bar and then the room behind, and from there I remember him saying -- he said the two of them should be removed, the voice said, and then Ramiz responded very angrily to what had been said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll just take -- go back to your last answer. I'll take it bit by bit. You said you heard a voice saying the two of them should be removed. Who were the two that that person was referring to?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand, the two children who had survived were to be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just go back - and we all appreciate it's been a long time - but try and use direct speech as best as you can about what Ramiz said and what the other person or persons said.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: That they should be removed, liquidated, killed, in other words, so that there would be no witnesses; that's how I understood it. And Ramiz responded to this and he said, No way. Nobody should kill those children; it's not the children's fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did Ramiz do then?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: And they continued discussing those children. There was arguing about it. And Ramiz said, Make sure nothing happens to those children.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was in the room with Ramiz when he was talking about the children?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Ramiz, Zuka, Nihko were there in the vicinity, and I think Sefer Halilovic was there as well because his driver was outside with the jeep. His nickname was Mesar; he was his driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know Sefer Halilovic's voice in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing Sefer Halilovic on the base in Zuka's headquarters when that conversation in Zuka's office was occurring?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I concluded he was there because I saw his driver. If his driver was outside with his jeep, then I concluded he was inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why was that? What led you to conclude the fact that his driver was there, I mean that Mr. Halilovic might have been there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: That was the custom in our parts; where the driver was, there his superior was or if he had an escort, he would be around.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What time do Your Honours intend to take the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it depends on you, actually. Can you finish your direct in five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not in five; maybe about 10 to 15. I don't think I can do it in five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that will be too long because we have been sitting here for one hour and 25 minutes. Maybe you could take a break right now. So we'll resume at 25 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before the break, Mr. Arnautovic, you were telling the Trial Chamber about Ramiz Delalic meeting at Zuka's base and speaking to Zuka Nihko, and you think Mr. Halilovic was there at the time. Do you remember whether Commander Karic, the one who made the comment about throwing civilians in the river, was in the room with Ramiz when he was talking about the children?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that no, you don't remember; or no, he wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't there because after saying, Throw into the Neretva anybody who makes any noises, he didn't -- he wasn't around anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you return to Grabovica after you'd taken the children to Zuka's base? That was on the 10th of September.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the checkpoint still there when you returned?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: There was the checkpoint from before, but an additional checkpoint had been added to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was the additional checkpoint? Was it before coming from the road from Jablanica or after coming on the road from Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: If you take the road from Jablanica towards Grabovica, there's a bridge you had to cross and that's where the additional checkpoint was installed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there soldiers at this additional checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Zuka's men were at the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Since some of his units were accommodated close by, there were four or five of his men.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that additional -- that extra checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just stop one moment, please. Your Honour, again to ask the witness to speculate as to the purpose of is it is not much use. If he was told something by those people at the checkpoint --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the Prosecution just asked a question: What was the purpose of this additional checkpoint? It -- the witness might know something about the purpose or may not. We haven't come to the question whether this witness will speculate something or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's no use objecting after the -- after it's happened, Your Honour, and it may create an unfairness to the witness, not a deliberate one, I'm sure. It just has the position of asking the witness to answer something and Your Honours heard the objection. I understand what Your Honour says about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Since Mr. Re has agreed to put it in another way, so we'll go along with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, what, if anything, did you find out was the purpose of this additional checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was surprised to see that checkpoint. I couldn't understand what it was all about, but when I approached I heard what the soldiers were saying. The purpose of the checkpoint is to close off all access to Grabovica, to prevent anyone from going in or out because there had been an attempt by some journalist, some press team from the international community or -- protected by the UNPROFOR to penetrate. And then Bakic Munir, from Mostar had also tried to come in, the minister of police, but that was later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear whether or not the minister for police had been able to get access to Grabovica? You said he tried to get in. Do you know whether -- did you hear whether he was able to get in?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. Nobody entered because preparations for an operation were underway at the moment and nobody was able to enter Grabovica, apart from individual soldiers involved in the preparations had the authority to come in and out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've referred throughout your testimony to preparations for combat. Did you and your -- members of your unit in fact go into combat, either on the 10th or another day?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After that we did go into combat. We were supposed to walk a long way to Dreznica, and from Dreznica to that hill which we were supposed to attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that on the 10th of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, again I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Timing is important and somewhat more important in this. To put the 10th to him like that was not acceptable and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re, maybe you can ask which date is that instead of identifying the 10th of September to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The previous question I said was it either the 10th or another day and his answer was yes. I was attempting to clarify by saying was that the 10th. I was not attempting to lead, but I can certainly rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, on what day did you go into combat in relation to what you've just described?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: It's easier for me to place it in time because I was there. We set out that evening because we had a long walk ahead of us upstream along the Neretva River to Dreznica. So we walked all night.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that the same day - just to clarify this - that you saw the two boys in Grabovica and took them to Zuka's base?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: The operation was about to start and we left in the evening that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you stay that night?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: The fighting men left that night; I stayed behind. And they went on foot to Dreznica and I went to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying you stayed in Jablanica that night, that's the night of the 10th?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the night of the 11th, where did you stay then?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th I was in Grabovica because there was some more fighting men whom I needed to take care of in case they needed support or transportation, et cetera, or logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you stay on the night of the 11th of September?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I was in that house where I spent nights before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did you return --

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: The one that I marked with a 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise. When did you return to Grab -- sorry, to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: We returned to Sarajevo on the night of the 12th. I know that because the 13th is my birthday. So we went to Sarajevo in the night between the 12th and 13th and we arrived sometime in the evening, early evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were in Grabovica on the 11th. About what time did you get to Grabovica on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You gave evidence earlier of there being Croat villages or civilians in Grabovica when you arrived on the 8th of September. Were there any Croat villagers remaining or residents remaining in Grabovica when you returned on the 11th of September?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was anything said to you about what -- about where the Croat villagers had gone or what had happened to them?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. There was no discussion about that nor did I see any dead or wounded. It's just as if everyone had vanished.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Apart from what the boys, the two boys, had said about members of their family being killed, were you told about any other Croats from that village being killed in that same sort of period?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: When we found out that those people had been killed and when some inquiries had already been made, it looked as if they had all disappeared overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the checkpoint, the additional checkpoint you referred to earlier which Zuka's men were at, was that there when you returned on the 11th and left on the 12th in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: As we were leaving we left the checkpoint behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is whether that additional checkpoint, the one you told us about earlier, the one which Zuka's men were guarding, was that still there on the 12th when you left for Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was still standing as we left. The men at the checkpoint were still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did any military police accompany you and the other soldiers in the trucks from Sarajevo on the 7th and 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there any military police or military security service personnel in Grabovica when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't see any military police anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were your -- were the men in your units, the ones lined up by Mr. Karavelic and sent to Sarajevo, were you ever given -- were you given any specific directions or instructions in relation to the treatment of civilians in that particular operation in which you were to take part?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No mention was made before us of any civilians that we were supposed to transfer or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you given any instruction or training as to the appropriate treatment by soldiers of civilians, what you could and couldn't do, before you went to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. We had no training of that kind at all. Men who served before us we thought had more experience and would tell us. That's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you ever given -- when I say "you," your unit, the 9th Motorised Brigade, were you and other soldiers given any training in relation to the Geneva Convention or the treatment of civilians at any time before you went to Grabovica in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not. But we talked amongst ourselves and we knew that civilians were not supposed to be touched and that property was not supposed to be damaged. That's what we knew from talking to each other, but there was no one from the corps telling us anything specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you or to your knowledge other soldiers who were in Grabovica on the 8th, 9th, and 10th of September ever questioned or interrogated in September 1993 as to what may have happened or the deaths of the civilians in Grabovica in that period?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody was interrogated. I told you there was stories going around to the effect that we were moving forward, advancing when the order came to stop the entire operation. But those were informal conversations; nobody interrogated us officially.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you ever interrogated yourself about the deaths of civilians in Grabovica in September 1993? Were you ever asked what had happened at any time?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: When we were arrested on the 26th of October, that's when the military security asked us some questions about this and that. Do you know anything about anybody killing someone? Things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you know about crimes that may have been committed in the Sarajevo area before September 1993 by members of the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see any killings with my own eyes, but while Juka Prazina was around I heard stories that in Paska Polje [phoen] Serb civilians were being killed, that certain things did occur.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said certain things did occur. Did you hear of crimes committed by the 9th Motorised Brigade that didn't involve killings in the Sarajevo area before September 1993?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: As for our units I know very well that there were no crimes committed, because our commander, Ramiz Delalic, was very strict on the rules, including a ban on alcohol and everything else concerning his troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A little earlier you told the Trial Chamber that Sefer Halilovic's driver was at Zuka's base on the 10th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you know at the time about who Sefer Halilovic was?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't so very well-versed in ranks. I know that commander of the army was very high up and that corps commander was just a little lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of the name of the operation you were to participate in in the liberation of Mostar? What was its name?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I knew we were heading for Mostar, and later on I learned the name of the operation was Neretva 93 because our crossing point was Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you know about what the overall commander of this operation was? Were you told who it was; and if so, whose name was it?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I knew that the main control of this entire Neretva 93 Operation was in the hands of Halilovic. But we came directly under the control of Zulfikar Alispago.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who told you the main control was of the entire operation was in the hands of Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we had those friends and that corps, of whose involvement I was not aware in Herzegovina, and later on when the operation was stopped I heard that all sorts of things had been going on, even that Izetbegovic himself issued the order to discontinue the operation and go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear that Halilovic was the main controller of the operation before you went to Grabovica or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I knew from before, since it was already being said that the Bosnia and Herzegovina army was making a successful advance and that strikes were successfully being carried out on that side. It was in the papers and I knew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before you went to Grabovica in September 1993, had you seen or did you know what Sefer Halilovic looked like?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew what he looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you seen him before in person?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I saw him in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he was one of the people who was with Mr. Karic when Mr. Karic made his remark about throwing civilians into the river?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: All I know is that it was a group of five or six. Whether he was in that group, I cannot be sure because I was really paying attention to Vehbija Karic. And I know that people from the east Herzegovina Corps were around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Earlier you told us that the meeting of which Mr. Karic made his remark on the first day you got there, which was the 8th of September, is that -- did you make any diary notes or anything of the date at the time?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: As I was a logistics man, I kept records of the cigarettes, weapons, packed lunches, and so on. I have the last names of all the men. I kept records of what I had given to whom, but when I was arrested in 1993 all this was taken from me and destroyed. It was never shown anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you made a diary note as to Mr. Karic making his remark, the fact that he made that remark. Do you remember whether you recorded that anywhere at the time?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't write that down but I recall those words very well because no normal man would say what he had said. I have to put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You're giving evidence about this many years after the event. Are you sure it was that day or could it have been on another day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If that's not cross-examination, I'm surprised. It's clearly just an attempt to elicit a different answer from the one he originally got. It's cross-examination; he's not allowed to do it, and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe the witness has already answered the question in a very clear way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. Arnautovic. Mr. Arnautovic, can you give us a clear assurance - so that the rest of your evidence is to be viewed in the right light - that you didn't shoot any civilians yourself? Can you give us that assurance?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you didn't stand by and watch any get shot?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I can prove that. I guarantee it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I understand that. You understand why these questions have to be asked, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. But what you can say clearly is: You didn't kill anyone and you weren't involved in any of the killings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, I'm crackling here in the microphone. Just excuse me a moment and we'll fix it up. Now, not only that but you didn't participate in any cleaning up of bodies or any concealing of the crime, did you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. It's quite clear to you that at some stage somebody must have done some clearing up. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in my opinion somebody did do that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you made some efforts to ask about what had happened and who had done that clearing up when you came back to Grabovica with Ramiz. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't competent to do that. I was on ordinary logistics man, just an unimportant soldier. It wasn't up to me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand you're not in the military police or in military security and you didn't have the competence to do it. But you were there with there -- with Ramiz when he was asking questions. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fact, you came back with him to the village, yes?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And as far as you could see, when Ramiz first found out about what had happened to the young boy's family, he seemed to you, who know him pretty well, to be very upset. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you saw him effectively spring straight into action and try to find out what on earth had happened. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What was it that he did first of all when you first spoke to the kids and found out the terrible story?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: He lined up the men because the boys said they would recognise the perpetrator, so he lined them all up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And can you say -- I know that the Prosecutor asked you a question about this, but did he line them up in front of that white house which you stayed in a day earlier or a night earlier?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was to the right of the white house. He couldn't do it inside because there were a hundred or so men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And a few bombs inside the house, yes? Some weapons --

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Mattresses on the floor, not beds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry. I might have understood you. You used that white house to put your gear in the -- some of your equipment and things that you as a logistics officer had in control. Did I misunderstand that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Packed lunches, ammunition, cigarettes, and up to four men slept there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. I'll just get you to point out on a picture --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could the witness please be shown Prosecution Exhibit Number P7, and it's the photograph of the white house. Your Honours, I'm sorry, we don't have a picture as yet. Now I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, can I just ask: Do you have that picture of the white house in front of you there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Is it possible to see on that picture where the line-up took place?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the right-hand side where there is a branch, there is a meadow there, on the right-hand side looking at it from this vantage point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. All right. Would you mind just marking with a blue pen where the line-up took place, please.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: There are some bushes here, but this is the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You'll just have to excuse us again, Mr. Arnautovic, while this picture gets brought up in a way that we can see. Okay. Excellent. Yes. Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I offer that for tender?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI 171.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think there's any objections, so it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Arnautovic, you'll just have to forgive the occasional lapse off into technology here, but now I can ask you the questions. Doing the best you can, can you say what it was that Ramiz asked of these people who were lined up? What sort of questions did he ask them?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall he asked them what had happened, if anybody had seen or heard anything. And everybody said they hasn't seen anything, heard anything, nobody knew anything. They just said they heard shooting in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what -- did he press them with further questions? Did he say, How can this be right? You're all living in these houses, you're all 20 metres away from each other, how can you not possibly have seen and heard what went on? Is that the sort of question he asked? You understand those are my words.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak more in the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They all said that nobody had heard or seen anything except for some shooting in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you remember which individual soldiers it was who said, We heard shooting but we don't know anything else?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Elvedin Husic, as he was there that night, said that he had heard shooting, he had heard shots. And Hajric, the young man who was there but was killed later said the same, and he can't testify because he's dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. None of these soldiers at that time indicated to Ramiz that they'd seen any dead bodies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Nobody said anything or saw anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And just to be clear about that, none of them that they'd seen the dead body of a soldier in military uniform. Is that correct, too?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: The body of a soldier? No, nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fact, is today the first time you've heard anyone suggest that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: This is the first time I've heard anyone saying that a soldier had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, thanks for that. And it was quite obvious to you that Ramiz was concerned to protect these two young kids?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: He fought fiercely when we arrived in Jablanica. He said, Let nobody touch a hair of their head when we leave. I remember that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, there's a lot of things that are being said about Ramiz Delalic, but you actually know him. Could you tell us a bit about him and what sort of personality he is.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I can say that you couldn't find a better man anywhere. Everybody knows he's a good man. He was good to the men as well. He did not permit any alcohol, he did not permit anyone to go into battle drunk. If somebody was afraid to go into battle, he let them stay behind. He was very correct. Some individuals from the supreme command hated him, but that's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'll come to the enemies that he had later on, but he had a pretty strong attitude about drugs, too, didn't he? I mean illegal drugs, not --

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No drugs were ever used. He was always against drugs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And so far as you could see, the 9th Brigade units that were commanded by Ramiz Delalic were probably better behaved than a lot of the other units in Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: When men are on leave, nobody can supervise them, but when they are in the headquarters, then of course you can supervise them. You can't really control what they do when they're out on the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And as far as you could see, Ramiz Delalic kept discipline pretty tight in his units. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I have to ask you about some of the things -- you recall the Prosecutor here asked you some questions about criminality or crimes that may have been committed by the members of the 9th Brigade. Do you remember being asked those questions by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Today?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Today, ten minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I just want to clarify some of those things, if you don't mind. First of all, the 9th Brigade had to guard an important part of the front line in Sarajevo. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And at that time the enemy across the front line was the Serb -- the republic -- the forces of the Republika Srpska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Without going into the whole history of the siege of Sarajevo and everything that happened, the fact is that you and soldiers that you knew were very much afraid that if Sarajevo fell it would be a great catastrophe for the Bosniak people, possibly even the Croat people that lived there as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because you had seen Vukovar on the television, hadn't you, and what happened there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But Sarajevo would have been ten times worse had they entered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So you had to fight hard?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because we know that had they entered Sarajevo there would have been an unprecedented massacre there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In terms of armaments, at the time when you were fighting in Sarajevo with the 9th Brigade, was there an arms blockade imposed on the Bosnian army preventing it from getting arms from overseas?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I know we couldn't get any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in short, did the units of the 9th Brigade have to raise funds for running a cafe called the Rapsodija cafe?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: It was the brigade coffee bar, and the money that was made was given to the families of fighters who have been killed; or if possible, weapons were purchased so we could defend ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's what I'm getting at here, Mr. Arnautovic, the purchase of weapons. Was it the case that sometimes citizens who had some money would - for example, local businessmen - make a donation to the 9th Corps in order to help -- sorry, to the 9th Brigade in order to help pay for weapons and for the needs of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: There was an association of independent businessmen, and they collected donations among themselves. Then they gave us stoves so we could keep warm and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when people from those businesses gave donations, whether in cash or in goods, was it the practice of the 9th Brigade to give them a receipt?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: They gave us those things. They didn't bring money to the brigade. They gave us stoves, food, uniforms, clothing. That was an association of independent businessmen, people who had their own shops and so on, and they brought money to a single collection point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And generally speaking -- well, I won't ask you generally, I'll put the specific question to you. Was there a need to dig trenches on the front line?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the front line was established at the beginning and then it moved. There were volunteers who dug trenches and the soldiers dug trenches. And Ramiz Delalic dug trenches personally. I myself avoided having to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I was about to come to that. Again, you know that there's been a lot said in the newspapers about trench-digging and about citizens being taken to dig trenches, but I want to ask you about the truth of it because you were there. Were most of the trenches there dug by the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the trenches in our brigade, yes. If there were any citizens they were volunteers and they were given the best conditions because we had a line of men in front protecting them. And there were people who didn't want to fight but who wanted to volunteer to dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And when people -- when civilians were digging trenches as far as you know, were they taken to the front line to dig trenches or were they at a position further back behind the lines?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Behind the front lines. Had you been able to go behind the lines, then we would have gone there as soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, I understand that. Now, I just have a couple of other questions about the 9th Brigade generally. You were in the zone of responsibility of the 1st Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the brigade itself had about 4.500 men in it, maybe approaching 5.000?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And it had what was sometimes called an attack company or a storm company. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And during your time there, the attack company was led by a man called Malco Rovcanin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And that attack company was one which was -- a unit that was able to be deployed at different sections of the front line and was sometimes used in emergencies to save situations at different sections of the front line. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: When there was heavy fighting or when a breakthrough was necessary, they were the first to go and get killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And in that capacity, for example, they went out to fight on Igman at the end of July in 1993. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When Igman fell, the corps sent us to Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: To protect Tesjan -- or rather Tresnjevo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Thanks very much. Okay. Now, at the time when this operation took place, you heard about it by being present at the 9th Brigade command with about 120 other people. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry. Pardon me. Let me ask you another question. You indicated earlier on that there was about 120 people gathered at the command post the day when Commander Karavelic came to give you your marching orders. Do you remember that day?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I remember there are about 120 men because they had to be collected from all the various units of our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on that occasion was there present -- were all the people there -- I take that back. Do you know an individual named Nihad Vlahovljak?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was he there on that day?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did he bring along some troops that you didn't personally know on that day?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I know there are about 120 fighters there who set out, but I didn't really look to see who was who.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm not criticising you for that, but I have to ask you the questions. You were asked earlier on about Mr. Sakrak. Do you recall whether you met Mr. Sakrak on that day or not?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say I met him. I simply cannot remember that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So is it safe to say this: That of those who set off on the 7th of September, there were some there that you just didn't know personally?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because they were from other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's the fact, isn't it, that -- I'm jumping forward a bit now, but by the time you got down to -- I'll withdraw that question. All right. Well, when you set off you had to walk to the tunnel. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you went through the tunnel and found your way to Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And at Hrasnica you were taken on board some trucks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: With a certain amount of difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let me just ask you about that certain amount of difficulty. Was it your initial understanding that Fikret Pravljak was supposed to provide some trucks on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: All I know is when we set out from the corps they said trucks would be waiting for us so we could continue our trip. However, when we arrived there were no trucks. And then we called Ramiz Delalic to get there and see for himself because originally he wasn't supposed to go to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And once he got there, did he come in the trucks with you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: When he arrived he had connections. He knew people among the Prevljaks and he sorted it out. It seems that the trucks had been delayed and they finally arrived. We boarded and went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you know whether those trucks came from the 6th Corps headquarters or not?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I didn't pay attention. The main thing for me was there was enough transportation for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. In the trucks -- all right. I've got some questions for you now about when you arrived at Zuka's base. That was about 8.00 in the morning. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Zuka personally came out and spoke to you -- to you, I mean Mr. Arnautovic, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: All of us fighters were around when he addressed us; it was right outside his headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, who was his logistics man?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I can't recall his name. It was something like Spaga or something like that. I saw him later. He was injured and he was disabled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But on this occasion he was -- it's a man called Spaga and he's operating as the logistics man for Zuka?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, when you were at Jablanica it's the fact, isn't it, that Zuka detailed an individual to take you to leave your trucks in fact off to Grabovica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Their men started from there. They were driving the trucks and they did everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. So it was really Zuka's unit that got you down to Grabovica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when you -- when the trucks pulled up in a Grabovica it was Zuka's men who pointed you out, the houses and the areas that you were to go to. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: They brought us to the place I showed in the pictures and they told us, This is where you are going to stay; this is Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it when the soldiers got out of the buses, they just behaved themselves properly and didn't shoot guns or behave in a silly way. Is that correct? Is that right, sorry?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. They were tired. They just sat around. Some of them went off to the river to wash themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And just on that question of firing off guns, no such thing happened. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. There was no shooting, there was no need to shoot because we were very close to the place where combat was supposed to begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. Okay. And in fact, prior to the time that you saw the two poor young boys, you personally didn't see any silly behaviour, shooting of guns, or other misbehaviour. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: That day when we found the boys, there was no shooting. It was not allowed to shoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What about the day before when you were coming backwards and forwards from Jablanica, did you notice any bad behaviour or shooting or carrying generally on that day?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, unless something happened while I was away that day in Jablanica. But while I was around I didn't see any carrying on or any shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. And I take it you yourself were quite upset when you heard the story that the two young boys had to tell?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, of course I was upset. I have children myself, because my own child suffered a terrible injury in an explosion and remained disabled. I -- the feeling I had was a terrible one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. So really, can you just explain to us perhaps that on that day, the 9th - that's the day when you're going backwards and forwards from Jablanica to Grabovica, and I think you indicated you did that several times - could you say approximately how many times you went backwards and forwards? Would it have been one or two? Would it have been five or six? Would it have been about ten? What's the best estimate that you can give?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Two or three times maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did those trips involve you going to Jablanica, collecting various types of goods, bringing them back, and distributing them to the soldiers back in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I only went for supplies. I would go over there, have certain supplies issued to me, take them back, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. You said two or three times. Were they -- was that two or three times in the morning, two or three times in the afternoon? We're talking about the 9th of September here. Or was it once or twice in the morning and once in the afternoon? How was it?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I went once in the morning -- in fact, more than once. But usually I went more than once a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm just restricting it to the 9th at the moment as I indicated in the previous question. Is the position this: That on the 9th you drove into Jablanica on two occasions and collected goods and brought them back to Grabovica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: On the 9th I went there and back and I spent the night in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. I haven't got to the night yet. I'm just sticking with the morning of the 9th if that's okay. Now, you've indicated already, I think, that you came and went twice in the morning. Now, just tell me: When you came back from Jablanica on those occasions, what did you do with the goods that you were bringing from Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I would leave them at the house where I stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you have any help unloading those goods into the house that you stayed in?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I had some fighting men around. I had that man Hajric, who later got killed, he would give me a hand if I needed anything. And while I was away, he would stand in there for me, issue things out, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did anyone else help you on that occasion -- on those occasions on the morning of the 9th of September? Any other soldiers help you to unload your jeep and put the things into the white house?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was usually the soldiers I mentioned because I was quite capable of handling it myself. It was not that it concerned huge amounts of equipment or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Arnautovic, you know it's important to come here and tell the truth, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you haven't come here to conceal anything or to paint a false picture, have you?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: No need.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I understand that. You know -- you knew what Sefer Halilovic looked like in September of 1993 because you'd seen him before in Sarajevo. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you'd seen him on television. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As far as you knew, he was the commander of the Bosnian army. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And he had been for over a year. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Until Rasim Delic came.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And in fact, more than that. You knew his driver. You knew what his driver looked like. That's Mesar; correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I knew what his driver looked like back from Mount Igman where I had seen him earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand all that. But the fact of the matter is this: That you saw Mr. Karic make what you've described as a bad comment in front of the soldiers on the 8th; correct? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you were standing less than 20 metres away from him. Right?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how many metres, but I was close by.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, were you as close as you are now to the Judges in this court. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
