utterances.text: Not that close, but okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Look, I'm putting this to you: Although you expressed some doubt to the Prosecutor earlier on, the fact of the matter is this: Sefer Halilovic just was not present when Karic made this comment that you ascribed to him. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say that I saw him there. I can't say that I saw him or that I remembered it clearly. All I know is that there was this Vehbija Karic and people from the corps and that's all I can remember for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me help you then. The people from the corps, do you remember -- I'll suggest some names to you and you tell me if that's accurate. A man called Zicro Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: That rings a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Rifat Bilajac?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translations continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: A driver from Zuka's unit called Huso Alic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I clarify something. The question seems a little bit unclear. Is my learned friend asking if he knows of these people or whether those people were present when Mr. Karic made his remark. I think there might be some confusion between the question and the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It will be clarified. Your Honour, I'll make that clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have to remind you that our time for this morning is up. Are you going to finish your -- this question or we'll start --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I can complete this question so that we don't labour tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This is the final question for the day, Mr. Arnautovic. And the question is this: Having heard those names Bilajac, Suljevic, Jankovic, and Alic, do you recall as you sit there now in court seeing those individuals?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I remember there were five or six men, and I remember Vehbija Karic clearly, and I'm sure he was there. I am only saying what I'm absolutely certain of. I am not willing to say anything else. I'm quite intent on saying and speaking only about the things I saw, despite some threats even that I received before coming here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you tell the police about these threats that you received?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: I don't need to talk to the police. I'm only afraid of God. And the people who stoop to threatening witnesses, it's their problem. There were telephone calls I received and I was warned of certain things in other ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you tell the Prosecutors about these telephone calls?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Which one did you tell of the people sitting over there?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, when I got that call, the first call in Sarajevo I informed the people who were right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... which Prosecutor did you tell about this, please, answer the question?

utterances.speaker: ERDIN ARNAUTOVIC
utterances.text: This gentleman here. I don't know his name, the one who's sitting right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm -- I'd just like as my final point to note who the witness is indicating there, and I think it would be common ground that he's indicating Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I'm sorry that we could not finish the testimony for today and you have to stay here for another day. As I did to other witnesses, that during your stay in The Hague you are still under the oath, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before you adjourn, just two very short matters I wish to raise, firstly is in terms of planning the witnesses for this witness. The next witness, of course, will be Mr. Mehanovic followed by Mr. Sakrak. On present indications, could the Defence possibly indicate whether we will get to Mr. Mehanovic tomorrow and Mr. Sakrak on Wednesday. That's point one. Point two is the fourth witness on the list this week, as Mr. Morrissey alluded to before, we will be making an application for protective measures which will be face distortion and a pseudonym, those are the measures we will be asking for. Possibly we will make the application tomorrow. I will inform my learned colleague this afternoon of the basis of the application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And of course we need written submissions of the list of the witnesses for this week. So the hearing is adjourned for this morning, and we'll resume tomorrow afternoon in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of February, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
